Step 2 of this card offered two routes; both were measured unworkable as written (2026-10-23, objectui `main` `2c4e5f5`):

- the `workflow_dispatch` route rests on a premise that does not hold: `ci.yml`'s `on:` is `push` / `pull_request` / `merge_group` / `schedule` only, and six of the queue's seven required contexts (`Lint` aside) come from workflows that take no `workflow_dispatch` (`ci.yml`'s `Type Check`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Test`; `changeset-presence.yml`'s `Changeset Declaration`; `governed-surface-guard.yml`'s `Governed Surface Queue Guard`);
- the relay route has no caller: the objectstack fleet-write relay starts only on a `repository_dispatch` to objectstack, which this repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot send, and no workflow here holds an App credential.

Step 1 is done: the relay's `pr_update_branch` synced #13028 as the fleet (head `17b3796`), every required context went green, and the seat's record is on #13028.

**Ruled: the refresh mints a narrowed, short-lived fleet App token on its runner (`actions/create-github-app-token`, the organization's `OS_FLEET_APP_ID` variable and `OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY` secret, scoped to this one repository) and pushes its branch and opens or updates its pull request with it, so the pull request's own events start CI.**

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): Sales (`os-sales`), the project owner directing this lane, in the project chat on 2026-10-23, replying to the coordinator's two-option summary (the App-token route vs. an objectstack-side upstream route with this card parked). Verbatim reply, untranslated:

> A

Two things this ruling cannot settle, asked of the maintainers (`GOVERNED_APPROVERS`) here; the implementing pull request stays a draft and waits for them:

1. **Secret visibility.** Is the organization secret `OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY` (and variable `OS_FLEET_APP_ID`) visible to `objectstack-ai/objectui`? A session cannot read an organization secret's repository access. If it is restricted to selected repositories, adding objectui is the one settings action this needs.
2. **Narrowing objectui#5397.** That ruling (2026-08-22) rejected "a PAT / GitHub App token" for the release pull request because a zero-trust-surface alternative existed there (validate the post-version tree in-workflow). This card has no such alternative: the refresh pull request exists so the new split runs the full suite before it lands. Confirm that #5397's rejection is read as scoped to the release pull request, so this workflow may mint the fleet token. A personal access token stays out either way.

Approving the implementing pull request answers both.
